label: La Gran Migración
summary: After the Second World War, hundreds of thousands of Puerto Ricans flew from San Juan to New York, building communities in East Harlem, the Lower East Side and the Bronx.

label: Windrush generation
summary: From 1948, when the Empire Windrush docked at Tilbury, Caribbean migrants, many from Jamaica, settled in London and brought sound systems, carnival and new music with them.

label: From sound system to hip hop
summary: DJ Kool Herc moved from Kingston to the Bronx in 1967, bringing Jamaican sound-system practice with him; his 1973 party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue is widely cited as hip hop's starting point.

label: Cuban exile
summary: Since the 1959 revolution, waves of Cubans have left for Miami, making Little Havana the centre of exile life.

label: Mariel boatlift
summary: Between April and October 1980, about 125,000 Cubans crossed from the port of Mariel to South Florida.

label: From Haiti to Little Haiti
summary: From the 1970s, Haitians settled in Miami and built Little Haiti into the centre of Haitian life in South Florida.

label: Hip hop crosses the Atlantic
summary: From the early 1980s, records, films and touring crews carried hip hop from New York to London, where it met the city's sound-system culture and fed later British forms, grime among them.

label: Latin music industry exchange
summary: Since the 2000s, Miami has been a major centre of the Latin music business, and many Puerto Rican artists, producers and labels work between San Juan and Miami.

label: WAVEMAKERS: Puerto Rico to New York
summary: Planned journey of the opening WAVEMAKERS chapter: the first leg, from San Juan to New York. In development; no episodes released yet.

label: WAVEMAKERS: New York to London
summary: Planned journey of the opening WAVEMAKERS chapter: the second leg, from New York to London. In development; no episodes released yet.
